A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SemVink method and HC-Bench study. All 10 pages of v1 and 11 pages of v3 are readable, including figures, tables, and references. Neither PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original HC-Bench evaluations of 11 VLMs, resolution and squint experiments, and embedding analyses in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds o3 results and evaluation on 53 independently collected internet images.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 retains aspect-ratio-preserving downscaling and the same brightness, contrast, and enhancement operations. Reordering zoom-out and squint descriptions and explicitly calling their integration inference-time do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds an independently collected set of 53 internet-sourced hidden-content images, extending evaluation beyond the authors' 112 generated HC-Bench images. This substantially broadens source coverage for the central task, although the PDF does not establish that the internet images are non-synthetic.

E2.justification: The main comparison adds o3, increasing coverage from 11 to 12 VLMs. The other comparators remain: the shortened Doubao table label corresponds to the full model name retained in Section 4.1. Newly cited preprocessing methods are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added 53-image validation uses the five existing evaluation conditions and reports one accuracy per model and condition. Existing HC-Bench scoring, prompting procedures, resolution ranges, and squint settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 4.3 and Table 5 directly investigate whether failure and recovery with zoom-out are artifacts of the generated benchmark. This adds a substantial independent-source robustness check. The existing resolution, squint, failure-case, and embedding analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experiments. The green numerical additions beside accuracy scores represent gains over baselines, not uncertainty estimates; v3 retains this reporting practice.

E6.justification: All 11 retained models' HC-Bench scores are unchanged between v1 Table 2 and v3 Table 4. The new o3 row reports 0% without zoom-out and 100% with it. New Table 5 reports 84.90–98.11% with zoom-out versus 0–3.77% across other conditions on the independent images; these are additional results, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The embedding-redundancy definition using cosine similarity above 0.95 is retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the added discussion of filtering and preprocessing does not introduce mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: v3 removes the introduction's claim that HC-Bench is the first hidden-content benchmark and updates the stated evaluation breadth from 11 to 12 models. The main claims about perceptual limitations, effective downscaling, and redundant embeddings remain.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the independent-image results as showing that failure is inherent to VLMs rather than dataset-specific. Its rewritten discussion explicitly acknowledges the existing Qwen2-VL-7B squint success and qualifies visual tools' ability to detect hidden adversarial triggers. The principal mechanism explanation and limitations remain.

D1.justification: The generation recipe, ControlNet weights, source resolutions, hardware, and project access information are substantively retained. The inference-time wording clarifies the already described preprocessing role. The new internet-image experiment provides no detailed collection procedure or release instructions.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning through new Section 2.4 on low-level operations, relating SemVink to anti-aliasing, AugMix, RandAugment, and adversarial input transformations. It also discusses earlier illusion studies by Hemmat, Rostamkhani, and Yichi Zhang and colleagues, alongside withdrawing the first-benchmark claim.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language edits, rewrites the discussion, merges the previous evaluation subsections, and reorders the zoom-out and squint descriptions. It adds a related-work subsection and acknowledgements while preserving the overall narrative and most existing prose.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 5 and an o3 row, reorders the existing results tables, restyles Figures 2 and 3, and adds explanatory answer labels and captions. Existing visual examples and embedding plots remain; these are localized presentation changes rather than a comprehensive redesign.

improvement.justification: The independent-image experiment provides useful evidence beyond the authors' generated benchmark, while expanded related work and removal of the first-benchmark claim improve positioning. These gains are limited by sparse documentation of the new collection and an overly strong inference that it rules out dataset-specific bias. The core method and existing results remain unchanged.
